definitions.explanation: A highly polite way to refer to someone else's name — used almost exclusively in writing, on forms, and at formal ceremonies. Common on wedding guest books, condolence registers, reception sign-in sheets, and formal invitations.

examples.japanese: ご{芳名|ほうめい}をお{書|か}きください。
{受付|うけつけ}でご{芳名|ほうめい}をご{記入|きにゅう}ください。
examples.english: Please write your name at the reception desk.

examples.japanese: {披露宴|ひろうえん}の{会場|かいじょう}には、ご{芳名|ほうめい}{帳|ちょう}が{置|お}かれ、{出席者|しゅっせきしゃ}が{順番|じゅんばん}に{名前|なまえ}を{記|しる}していた。
examples.english: A guest book was placed at the wedding reception, and the attendees were writing their names in turn.

notes:
Composed of the beautifying / honorific prefix ご〜 + {芳名|ほうめい} ("fragrant/esteemed name"), a classical-feeling compound of {芳|ほう} (fragrant; a polite adjective for another's things) and {名|めい} (name). The literal "fragrant name" metaphor signals deep respect for the person whose name is being asked for.

USAGE:
- Used to refer to the addressee's name respectfully in very formal written contexts. Ordinary polite conversation uses お{名前|なまえ} (your name) instead.
- Appears most often on forms and registers where guests are asked to write their names: {芳名|ほうめい}{帳|ちょう} (guest book), {芳名|ほうめい}{録|ろく} (register of names).
- Common at weddings, funerals, opening ceremonies, exhibition openings, and other formal events. On an invitation, ご{芳名|ほうめい} may be used to respectfully refer to the invitee's name.
- When using ご{芳名|ほうめい} about your own name, you must drop the ご〜 and ideally avoid {芳名|ほうめい} altogether — use {お名前|おなまえ} or {名前|なまえ} for your own.

FORMALITY NOTE:
- This word belongs to highly formal written Japanese; it is out of place in ordinary conversation. In most spoken settings, お{名前|なまえ} is the natural polite choice.
- Common invitation-card politeness rule: when RSVPing, guests often cross out the ご before {芳名|ほうめい} on their returned card as a gesture of humility toward their own name.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ご{芳名|ほうめい}をお{書|か}きください: please write your name
- ご{芳名|ほうめい}をご{記入|きにゅう}ください: please fill in your name
- ご{芳名|ほうめい}{帳|ちょう}: guest book / register
- ご{芳名|ほうめい}{録|ろく}: register of names (formal, for ceremonial events)
- ご{芳名|ほうめい}を{賜|たまわ}る: to kindly receive (someone's) name (very formal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{名前|なまえ}: your name — the standard polite term; used in everyday polite speech and on most forms.
- ご{氏名|しめい}: your full name — formal; asks specifically for the full family-and-given name, commonly on official documents.
- {御名前|おなまえ}: polite, written variant of お{名前|なまえ}; essentially the same in meaning.
